query: What signals are linked to longer resolution duration values?

per_column.name: incident_type
per_column.rationale: Categorizing incidents by type gives a genuine grouping axis to compare resolution durations across issue kinds. Values are soundly derived from short_description in all samples.

per_column.name: infrastructure_target
per_column.rationale: Well-grounded in the description text, but largely a near-restatement of incident_type (wifi->wifi_network, vpn->vpn, database->database), reducing its independent analytical leverage for this query.

per_column.name: assigned_technician
per_column.rationale: Technician-level grouping could relate to resolution time, but this appears redundant with the existing closed_by/assigned_to columns. More seriously, values contradict the source: rows with closed_by 'Charlie Whitherspoon' and 'Luke Wilson' produced 'beth_anglin' and 'charlie_whitherspoon', indicating unsupported/invented assignments.

per_column.name: technician_handoff
per_column.rationale: A handoff flag is a plausible signal for longer durations, but the samples give no textual basis (only opened_at, closed_by shown) for asserting True/False, and it depends on the unreliable assigned_technician; values look inferred without support.

per_column.name: caller_type
per_column.rationale: Distinguishing named vs itil users is a reasonable grouping axis, but the source samples don't expose caller_id and the two VPN rows get different caller_types without visible justification, suggesting weakly grounded values.

per_column.name: issue_scope
per_column.rationale: Scope (single_user vs building_wide) is a strong candidate driver of duration. However 'Printing issues in office' -> 'floor_specific' and VPN -> 'infrastructure_component' are confident specifics the text does not clearly warrant, indicating partial invention.

per_column.name: severity_signal
per_column.rationale: A bare boolean severity flag adds limited leverage and partly overlaps with the existing priority column. Values are plausible but the text basis is thin; no clear contradiction observed in samples.

per_column.name: issue_complexity_signal
per_column.rationale: Complexity is directly relevant to resolution duration and offers a good modeling axis. But low/medium/high assignments (e.g. VPN->medium, database->low) are confident gradations not clearly derivable from the short descriptions, so groundedness is moderate.

judge.rationale: Several columns (incident_type, issue_scope, issue_complexity_signal) provide genuine new axes relevant to explaining resolution duration. However groundedness is uneven: assigned_technician directly contradicts the visible closed_by values, and technician_handoff, caller_type, issue_scope, and complexity include confident specifics the sampled source text does not support. A few columns (infrastructure_target, severity_signal) also add limited independent leverage due to redundancy with incident_type and priority.
